Income
With agriculture dominating the economy, 1970 census data indicates family income for Big Horn County was made up of $12,824,500 from wages and salaries (including wages for farm hands), $3,561,300 from farm self-employment, and $1,206,900 from non-farm self-employment. Family income in the Sarpy Census Division in Big Horn County, a census division typical of the Westmoreland Resources lease area, consisted of $486,200 from wages and salaries (including wages for farm hands), and $307,700 from farm self-employment.
Income, expressed on a per capita basis, is shown graphically in Figure II-11.
Income levels of Big Horn and Treasure County residents are lower than those of Montana or the nation, while the income of the Indians on the Crow Reservation is substantially lower still.
